key_insight: A temporal attention-based multimodal deep learning model can detect hard-to-see welding defects in real time with strong interpretability.
engineering_relevance: This enables faster, more reliable in-process quality control for fillet joint welding, reducing post-weld inspection, repairs, and production delays.
method: Trained on synchronized welding images and acoustic data from an industrial collaborative welding robot.
Used a temporal attention deep learning architecture to classify internal defects such as porosity, lack of penetration/fusion, undercut, and cold lap.
Applied explainable AI to identify important image/spectrogram regions and assess which modality best supports each defect type.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the attention module improved performance to an F1 score of 0.99 on the collected welding dataset.
watch_item: Model performance may depend on the specific robot, sensor setup, and defect distribution, so transfer to other welding lines likely requires revalidation and calibration.
paper_title: Explainable Temporal Attention-based Defect Detection For Fillet Joints in Real-Time Gas Metal Arc Welding Based on Multi-modal Data
